To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

N-substituted analogs of benzo-tropine (BzT) possess high-affinity binding at dopamine (DA) transporters, block DA uptake, and produce behavioral effects similar to those of cocaine in some tests but not in others.

N-substitutions of benztropines (BZTs) with reduced muscarinic affinity reduce cocaine-like effects in dopamine transporter ligands, suggesting that muscarinic antagonism may contribute to cocaine-like effects in BZTs.
N-substitution of benztropines (BZT), a cocaine-like compound with reduced muscarinic M-1 receptor affinity, reduces cocaine-like effects in mice and rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of compounds that bind to the dopamine transporter and inhibit dopamine uptake, and yet have effects different from those produced by cocaine.
the identification of novel compounds that may serve as potential medications to treat cocaine addiction.
the design and synthesis of novel compounds with high affinity and specificity for the dopamine transporter (DAT), the target for the psychostimulant cocaine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
N-substituted 4′, 4′-difluoro-benztropine analogues have been synthesized and evaluated as dopamine transporter ligands.
the BZT analogues are not cocaine like, and the M1 receptor is not a major factor in the cocaine-like effects of cocaine.
N-substitutions in the 4′, 4′′ position of BZT analogues reduce the affinity at muscarinic-M receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cocaine-like effects of BZT-analogues are reduced with N-substitution, but that the compounds still have high affinity for the DAT, suggesting that the compounds may be useful for the development of cocaine abuse medications.
the BZT analog AHN 1,055 has a cocaine-like action at the dopamine transporter but has a reduced ability to substitute for cocaine.
the N-substitution of 4,4′-diF-tropane compounds with alkyl or aryl substituents reduces M1 affinity and produces a compound with reduced cocaine-like effects.

we have identified a new series of compounds that are dopamine transporter ligands that are not cocaine-like.
